check: why the full GameTest run takes hours, and how long to budget after the stress profile
observedDiscrepancy: A 33-test diagnostic subset finished in 140 seconds, about 4.2 seconds per test. The recorded full run of 119 tests took 3h22m, about 102 seconds per test - a 24-fold difference that needed explaining before it could be used for planning.
explanation: The suite is not uniform. A handful of cases are combinatorial matrices rather than single assertions, and those dominate the wall-clock time.

heavyCases.AdjacentComponentMatrixTests: 8 cases with timeoutTicks=1000000; one enumerates 256 combinations from 8 kinds x 8 kinds x 2 profiles x 2 boundaries, asserted as cases.size() == 256
heavyCases.OracleGameTests: 5 cases, one with timeoutTicks=20000000, two orders of magnitude above the smallest
heavyCases.others: AdjacentFixtureDiagnosticTests, ComponentSurvivalMatrixTests, CurvedGateRegressionTests, CurvedSiteMatrixTests, CurvedWallMatrixTests, FringeOwnerCoverageTests, GroundEntranceContractGameTests, HydroBoundaryRegressionTests, NoiseBridgeGameTests, ProductionPipelineTests and RampGroundPortalTests all carry the same large timeout

batches.note: 11 explicitly named batches beyond the default, which is why the suite runs in a defined order rather than one flat pool.

budget.method: scaled by count, which is a rough estimate rather than a measurement; the new cases are cheap ones, so the true figure may be slightly lower

whyThisMatters: The post-stress schedule is GameTest then Test-S5Release.ps1, and Test-S5Release's two clean builds add up to two hours. Knowing the first is about 3.65 hours rather than tens of minutes is what makes the sequencing realistic.
